figures.caption: Fig. 1: UNSW-NB15 ablation results across window scales, reported in AUPRC. The x-axis corresponds to the ablation ladder H , A+H , A+H+V , A+H+S+V , and Full; the legend denotes the four window scales. The strongest clean evidence appears at 60 s, where the full macrostate is best.
TABLE IV: Symbolic dictionary for the macrostate framework.

Fig. 3: Multiscale fusion results on UNSW-NB15. Simple scorelevel and stacked fusion improve over the baseline regime, but they do not surpass the best single-scale macrostate model. This indicates that multiscale aggregation is useful, but not yet stronger than the best informative single-scale representation in the current setup.

Fig. 4: Two-dimensional PCA projection of the 60s UNSW macrostate representation. Benign and malicious windows exhibit partial but visible separation, supporting the claim that the learned macrostate induces a meaningful state-space rather than collapsing the classes into a single overlapping distribution.

Fig. 5: First-pass CIC-IDS2017 comparison at 30s and 60s using AUPRC. At both scales, the best macrostate model outperforms the best entropy-based baseline, while 60s is stronger overall. The differing best ablation stages across the two scales also indicate early scale sensitivity on CIC.
